sentences.text: 3. Heard Mr. Ankit Pandey, learned counsel for the  Applicants, Ms. Rajeshree Newton, learned APP for the  Respondent-State and Ms. Akanksha Pandey, learned counsel  for the informant.

4. On the last occasion vide order dated 22.2.2024,
 the Applicants and the original informant were referred for  mediation.
5. Today both learned counsel for the respective parties  are present before the Court.
The mediation report dated  10.4.2024 is also submitted by the learned Mediator.
The  report mentions that the parties had settled the case amicably  with their own wish and they have signed the consent terms  before the learned Mediator.
The consent terms signed by  both the parties are annexed to the mediation report.
6. Today, the informant is present in the Court.
He is  identified by the learned counsel representing him.
She, on  his instructions, states that the informant has no objection for  allowing this Application.

sentences.text:
In view of the consent terms and in view of the  averments made in clauses (k) and (x) of the consent terms  mentioning that the parties are agreeable for disposal of the  application, this Application can be allowed and the Applicants  can be granted anticipatory bail.
 8.
Before parting with the order, I record my  appreciation of the successful efforts put in by the learned  Mediator.

9. Hence, the following order :
 ORDER (i) In the event of their arrest in connection with C.R.No.429/2023 registered at Nerul Police Station, Navi Mumbai, the Applicants are directed to be released on bail on their furnishing PR bonds in the sum of Rs.30,000/- each (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one or two sureties each in the like amount.
(ii) Anticipatory Bail Application stands disposed of accordingly.
(SARANG V. KOTWAL, J.) Deshmane (PS) 3 of 3 PRADIPKUMAR PRAKASHRAO PRAKASHRAO DESHMANE DESHMANE Date:
